transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Ravi (CTO Helion), Sofia (Lead ML Eng), Tom (Infra)

[00:00] Aisha: Hi everyone  thanks for jumping on. Quick intros? I'm Aisha, account exec at Redwood.
[00:08] Ravi: Hey all, Ravi here, CTO at Helion. We're evaluating options for model infra, mainly to power in-app assistants and some customer support automation.
[00:15] Sofia: Sofia, lead ML. We're focused on throughput and cost, plus integration with our LangChain stacks.
[00:20] Tom: Tom, infra  I'll be looking at networking, VPC, and benchmark needs.
[00:26] Connor: Connor, SE with Redwood  I'll walk through SDKs and deployment patterns.

[00:35] Aisha: Great. high level, are you leaning hosted or self-hosted? What's driving the eval?
[00:40] Ravi: We're open. Primary constraints: data residency for EU customers, P95 latency target of ~120ms for short chats, and cost  we have a lot of tokens. Also SSO and audit needs for compliance.
[00:52] Sofia: Also we use LangChain heavily and LlamaIndex for vector stores; want minimal glue.

[01:05] Connor: Got it. Redwood supports hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). SDKs exist for Python/Node; we also have first-class LangChain adapters and a LlamaIndex connector sample.
[01:18] Sofia: Quick question: are those adapters maintained upstream or are they community?
[01:22] Connor: They're Redwood-maintained, we keep them up to date with LangChain releases. We provide example notebooks; I'll attach a LangChain notebook with Helion-like prompts.

[01:35] Ravi: For Hosted, how do you handle traffic egress and data retention  we can't send raw PII off-cloud for EU users without residency guarantees.
[01:44] Aisha: For EU-sensitive data we usually recommend Dedicated or Private  Dedicated can be region-locked and offer stronger isolation. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem. We have KMS integrations for encryption at rest.

[02:05] Tom: On Dedicated  does that sit behind our corporate gateway? We have an existing API gateway (Kong) and identity proxy.
[02:12] Connor: Yes. You can front Redwood with your gateway or use our gateway/proxy mode. Many customers put a lightweight sidecar or proxy to implement rate limiting and request enrichment. We have examples for Kong, Envoy.

[02:30] Tom: Are there any differences in observability hooks across modes? We need trace context, token-level cost metrics, and audit logs forwarded to our Splunk.
[02:38] Connor: All modes provide trace headers and per-request metadata. Dedicated/Private let you ship audit logs to your S3/ELK/Splunk via secure connectors. Hosted can export logs too but retention tiers differ. We'll share the exact schema.

[02:55] Sofia: On SDKs  do you provide streaming and function calling in the same SDKs? Our stack uses streaming for UI snappiness.
[03:01] Connor: Yes, our Python and Node SDKs support streaming, tool-calling primitives, and structured output. We also have LangChain chains that wire up streaming tokens to UI websockets. Example notebook will demo streaming with a small web UI.

[03:20] Ravi: Token billing  do you provide accurate token counts client-side? We need predictable cost models and quota enforcement.
[03:27] Aisha: We bill per-token for hosted; Dedicated is usually commit-based with usage reconciliation. We expose token-level metrics in the Console so you can map routes to cost. Quotas and rate limits can be applied at token or request level.

[03:45] Tom: How are rate limits implemented? If we front you with our gateway, do you still enforce per-customer quotas?
[03:52] Connor: Yes  you can enforce at multiple layers. If you use your gateway you can do edge rate limiting. Redwood's platform can apply per-API-key quotas, per-route caps, and burst policies. For Dedicated we can also configure autoscaling and reserved throughput so you don't hit soft limits.

[04:10] Sofia: About LlamaIndex  our retrieval pipeline uses combined embeddings and re-ranker. Does Redwood provide embedding endpoints or do we host embeddings ourselves?
[04:18] Connor: We offer embeddings via the API. Many customers use Redwood embeddings for index creation then store vectors in their chosen vector DB. We also support batched embedding calls and a caching layer to reduce cost.

[04:35] Ravi: Can you talk about gateway/proxy pattern in more detail? We're trying to avoid double-rate limiting and want consistent auth via our IdP.
[04:42] Connor: Typical pattern: you front Redwood with your gateway for auth (SSO/JWT) and request shaping. Gateway forwards a sanitized request to Redwood with a signed proxy token. Alternatively, you can use Redwood's sidecar that does automatic key rotation and mTLS to the control plane. We have a sample repo for Kong and for an Envoy sidecar.

[05:05] Tom: mTLS and KMS  for Private, can we bring our own HSM?
[05:11] Aisha: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. We'll need to scope connectivity and provisioning; that's usually part of the Private onboarding.

[05:30] Ravi: On latency  we need p95 120ms for short prompts. What's realistic for hosted vs dedicated?
[05:38] Connor: For hosted, latencies vary by model and region; small models in the same region can meet 80120ms p95 for short tokens if below concurrency thresholds. Dedicated with reserved GPU pools gets you more predictable p95 and better isolation. For strict SLOs, Dedicated or Private is recommended. We'll run benchmarks against your prompt shapes.

[05:58] Sofia: Are there recommended quantization profiles? We use some Llama variants and want to reduce cost.
[06:03] Connor: Yes  Redwood Optimize recommends quantization and kernel selection based on model and input length. For Llama2-family we often suggest 4-bit quantization profiles that keep quality high but cut cost. We'll include those recommendations in the notebook.

[06:20] Ravi: For the integration path, here's roughly what we want: quick PoC using Hosted to validate quality, then Dedicated in region for EU traffic, and Private for certain regulated customers. Timeline: validate by end of Q1.
[06:33] Aisha: Sounds reasonable  many customers do Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private as they scale. For PoC we can provision a short-lived Dedicated test pool or run a hosted eval with higher retention.

[06:50] Tom: One operational question  if we route through our gateway, does Redwood still see original headers for tracing? We want full trace correlation.
[06:58] Connor: Yes, we pass through trace headers (W3C traceparent) and you can send back trace ids in responses. Our Console can ingest trace spans; many customers correlate with Jaeger/Zipkin and Splunk. There may be sampling options for high volumes.

[07:15] Sofia: Error handling: if Redwood falls back to a smaller model for cost, do you provide signal so we can detect quality regressions?
[07:23] Connor: We expose model variant metadata per response and have rollout policies. You can set automatic fallbacks with tags so your app can detect and switch. We also support quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and have regression alerts.

[07:40] Ravi: Security review  we'll need SOC2, ISO docs, network diagrams, pen test results. Also SSO (SAML), RBAC, and audit logs retention policy.
[07:50] Aisha: We'll send the full security pack. For Dedicated/Private we can provide network diagrams and for Private, customer-managed control plane details. I'll include SAML and RBAC docs and our standard audit log retention options.

[08:05] Tom: Any prebuilt observability webhooks for token-level billing or do we scrape the Console?
[08:12] Connor: We provide both. Console has token-level dashboards and you can export via API/webhooks to your internal billing. You can also stream events to your S3 or Kafka for long-term analysis.

[08:28] Sofia: About LangChain examples  do you have chains for retrieval augmented generation with streaming and retry logic?
[08:34] Connor: Yes  chains for RAG, re-ranker integration, streaming to UI, and automatic retry/backoff. We'll attach the example that wires LangChain -> Redwood SDK -> Redis/Vector DB.

[08:50] Ravi: One more: SLA for Dedicated? Uptime and latency guarantees?
[08:56] Aisha: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on commit tier. We'll include sample SLA language in the pricing doc.

[09:10] Tom: If we go Private on-prem, how long is typical onboarding?
[09:16] Connor: On-prem Private is typically 610 weeks including network, KMS, and onboarding. VPC-managed Private can be faster (36 weeks) depending on approvals.

[09:32] Sofia: For the PoC, we'd like an example that shows: LangChain agent calling tools, streaming tokens, observability hooks, and a small benchmark comparing hosted vs dedicated.
[09:41] Connor: We can build that. We'll prepare a repo and a notebook with a small web UI and a benchmark harness.

[09:52] Ravi: Are there rate limit primitives for bursty traffic? Our traffic is spiky during product launches.
[09:58] Connor: Yes  burst tokens and burst windows configurable. For Dedicated you can set reserved throughput and burst buckets so you don't get throttled. We also have queueing options for smoothing spikes.

[10:12] Aisha: Ok let's capture next steps  I'll read them back after a quick few more questions.

[10:20] Sofia: Slight nit  what about schema enforcement for structured outputs? We rely on JSON schema outputs from models.
[10:26] Connor: Redwood supports structured output validation and function/tool calling that enforces schema. We can validate and reject responses that don't match schema and surface errors to your app.

[10:40] Ravi: Great. Any known gotchas with LangChain versions? We run a slightly older LangChain at the moment.
[10:47] Connor: We'll note compatibility matrix in the notebook; most adapters support a range but we'll include notes for older LangChain versions and a migration path.

[10:58] Tom: For the benchmark  what metrics will you collect?
[11:02] Connor: We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, concurrency behavior, and memory/KV cache hit rates. We'll provide the raw CSV and a dashboard.

[11:18] Aisha: Okay let's do a short recap of next steps. Connor?
[11:22] Connor: I'll prepare the LangChain/LlamaIndex notebook, the gateway/proxy sample (Kong/Envoy), and the benchmark harness; share via GitHub.

[11:30] Aisha: I'll send pricing/commit options, the security pack, and propose times for the PoC benchmark (week of 12/21).

[11:36] Ravi: Tom and I will share traffic profiles and SLOs, and Sofia will give a sample prompt set and dataset for the notebook.

[11:48] Sofia: Quick note  include example for embedding cache and dedupe keys, that's important for cost.

[11:53] Connor: Will do.

[12:00] Aisha: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links.

[12:04] Ravi: Thanks.

[12:08] -- end --
